Document: Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents
Section: 5.9
Part 2 of 4
==================================================
## 5.9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9] (1) Where the claimant reasonably believes that the claim is valued at above the limit in paragraph (2) but at no more than the Protocol upper limit, but it subsequently becomes apparent that the value of the claim is below the limit in paragraph (2), the claimant is entitled to the Stage 1 and (where relevant) the Stage 2 fixed costs.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9] (2) The limit referred to in paragraph (1) above is £5,000 for damages for personal injury and £10,000 in total and is limited to claims where the claimant is not a child.

## 5.9A

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), where a claim has started in the RTA Small Claims Protocol and the defendant has notified the claimant that they consider the overall claim is likely to be valued at more than £10,000 or the claim for damages for injury is likely to be valued at more than £5,000, this Protocol should be applied starting at paragraph 6.1.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (2) Paragraph (1) applies only where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (a) the defendant also notifies the claimant that they consider that the claim is worth no more than the Protocol upper limit;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (b) the claim is not one which was started in the RTA Protocol and no longer continued in that protocol; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (c) either—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (i) there was an admission of liability in full under this Protocol within the response period;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (ii) there was an admission of liability in full but subject to an argument that the claimant contributed to their injuries by not wearing a seatbelt (where the claimant admitted not doing so); or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (iii) the period for a liability response under this Protocol has not yet expired.

## Claimants without a legal representative

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] 5.10 Where the claimant does not have a legal representative, on receipt of the CNF the defendant must—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] (1) explain the period within which a response is required;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] (2) explain that the claimant may obtain independent legal advice; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] (3) undertake a search of askCUEPI (website at: www.askCUE.co.uk (opens in a new tab) ) or an equivalent search system for defendants.

## 5.10A Where the claimant does not have a legal representative, paragraph 6.3A does not apply.

## Discontinuing the Protocol process

## 5.11 Claims which no longer continue under this Protocol cannot subsequently re-enter the process.

## SECTION III – THE STAGES OF THE PROCESS

## Stage 1

## Completion of the Claim Notification Form

## 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] (1) the CNF to the defendant’s insurer; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] (2) the ‘Defendant Only CNF’ to the defendant by first class post, except where the defendant is a self-insurer in which case the CNF must be sent to the defendant as insurer and no ‘Defendant Only CNF’ is required.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] 6.2 The ‘Defendant Only CNF’ must be sent at the same time or as soon as practicable after the CNF is sent.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] 6.3 All boxes in the CNF that are marked as mandatory must be completed before it is sent.  The claimant must make a reasonable attempt to complete those boxes that are not marked as mandatory.

## 6.3A

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (1) Before the CNF is sent to the defendant pursuant to paragraph 6.1, the claimant’s legal representative must undertake a search of askCUEPI (website at: www.askCUE.co.uk (opens in a new tab) ) and must enter in the additional information box in the CNF the unique reference number generated by that search.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (2) Where the claimant has sent the CNF without the unique reference number required by subparagraph (1), the defendant may require the claimant to resend the CNF with the reference number inserted. The period in paragraph 6.11 or 6.13 starts from the date the CNF was sent with the unique reference number.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (3) Where the claimant has sent the CNF without the unique reference number required by subparagraph (1) and the defendant does not require the claimant to resend the CNF pursuant to subparagraph (2), the defendant must respond in accordance with paragraph 6.11 or 6.13.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] 6.4 A claim for vehicle related damages will ordinarily be dealt with outside the provisions of this Protocol under industry agreements between relevant organisations and insurers.  Where there is a claim for vehicle related damages the claimant must—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (1) state in the CNF that the claim is being dealt with by a third party; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (2)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (a) explain in the CNF that the legal representative is dealing with the recovery of these additional amounts; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (b) attach any relevant invoices and receipts to the CNF or explain when they are likely to be sent to the defendant.

## 6.5 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.5 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.] 6.6 The statement of truth in the CNF must be signed either by the claimant or by the claimant’s legal representative where the claimant has authorised the legal representative to do so and the legal representative can produce written evidence of that authorisation. Where the claimant is a child the statement of truth may be signed by the parent or guardian. On the electronically completed CNF the person may enter their name in the signature box to satisfy this requirement.

## Rehabilitation

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Rehabilitation] 6.7 The claimant must set out details of rehabilitation in the CNF. The parties should at all stages consider the Rehabilitation Code which may be found at: http://www.iua.co.uk/IUA_Member/Publications (opens in a new tab)

## Failure to complete the Claim Notification Form

## 6.8

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.8] (1) Subject to subparagraph (2) and paragraph 6.3A(2), where the defendant considers that inadequate mandatory information has been provided in the CNF, that shall be a valid reason for the defendant to decide that the claim should no longer continue under this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.8] (2) Where the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant without the unique reference number required by paragraph 6.3A(1), but the defendant does not require the claimant to resend the CNF with the reference number inserted pursuant to paragraph 6.3A(2), the fact that the claimant has not provided this information shall not be a valid reason for the defendant to decide that the claim should no longer continue under this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.8] 6.9 Rule 45.35(2) and (3) sets out the sanctions available to the court where it considers that the claimant provided inadequate information in the CNF.

## Response from insurer

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Response from insurer] 6.10 The defendant must send to the claimant an electronic acknowledgment the next day after receipt of the CNF.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Response from insurer] 6.11 The defendant must complete the ‘Insurer Response’ section of the CNF (“the CNF response”) and send it to the claimant within 15 days.

## Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits] 6.12 The defendant must, before the end of Stage 1, apply to the Compensation Recovery Unit (CRU) for a certificate of recoverable benefits.

## Motor Insurers’ Bureau

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Motor Insurers’ Bureau] 6.13 Where no insurer is identified and the claim falls to be dealt with by the MIB or its agents the CNF response must be completed and sent to the claimant within 30 days.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Motor Insurers’ Bureau] 6.14 Where the MIB passes the claim to an insurer to act on its behalf, that insurer must notify the claimant of that fact. There is no extension to the time period in paragraph 6.13.

## Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] 6.15 The claim will no longer continue under this Protocol where the defendant, within the period in paragraph 6.11 or 6.13—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (1) makes an admission of liability but alleges contributory negligence (other than in relation to the claimant’s admitted failure to wear a seat belt);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (2) does not complete and send the CNF response;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (3) does not admit liability; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (4) notifies the claimant that the defendant considers that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (a) there is inadequate mandatory information in the CNF; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (b)  if proceedings were issued, the small claims track would be the normal track for that claim.

## 6.15A Where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (a) paragraph 6.15(4)(b) applies;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (b) the date of the accident is on or after 31 st May 2021; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (c) the parties have agreed that the RTA Small Claims Protocol applies,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] the claimant must start a claim by following that Protocol, starting at paragraph 5.3.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] 6.16 Where the defendant does not admit liability under paragraph 6.15(3), the defendant must give brief reasons in the CNF response.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] 6.17 Where paragraph 6.15 applies the claim will proceed under the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims starting at paragraph 6.3 of that Protocol (which allows a maximum of three months for the defendant to investigate the claim) except that where paragraph 6.15(4)(a) applies the claim will proceed under paragraph 5.1 of that Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (For admissions made in the course of the process under this Protocol, see rule 14.1B.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (Paragraph 2.10A of the Pre-Action Protocol on Personal Injury provides that the CNF can be used as the letter of claim except where the claim no longer continues under this Protocol because the CNF contained inadequate information.)

## Stage 1 fixed costs

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] 6.18 Except where the claimant is a child, the defendant must pay the Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 10 of Practice Direction 45 and, in a soft tissue injury claim, the cost of obtaining the fixed cost medical report and any cost for obtaining medical records in rule 45.62(2) (collectively the “Stage 1 fixed recoverable costs”) where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] (1) liability is admitted; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] (2) liability is admitted and contributory negligence is alleged only in relation to the claimant’s admitted failure to wear a seat belt, within 10 days after receiving the Stage 2 Settlement Pack, provided that invoices for the cost of obtaining the medical report and any medical records in a soft tissue injury claim have been included in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] 6.19 Where the defendant fails to pay the Stage 1 fixed recoverable costs within the period specified in paragraph 6.18 the claimant may give written notice that the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol. Unless the claimant’s notice is sent to the defendant within 10 days after the expiry of the period in paragraph 6.18 the claim will continue under this Protocol.

## Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims] 6.19A Where liability is admitted in a soft tissue injury claim, it is expected that in most cases the defendant’s account will not be relevant to the procedure in Stage 2. In the limited cases where it is considered appropriate, the defendant may send their account to the claimant electronically at the same time as the CNF response. The defendant’s insurer must have the defendant’s written authority to provide this account and, in sending it, is certifying that it has that authority. For the purposes of this paragraph, the defendant’s written authority may be provided electronically.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims] 6.19B The procedure in paragraph 6.19A applies to the MIB, save that the MIB is certifying that the defendant user of the vehicle has provided such authority.

## Stage 2

## Medical Reports – all claims

## 7.1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] (1) Save where paragraph (2) applies, the clamant should obtain a medical report, if one has not already been obtained.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] (2) In claims which consist of or include a whiplash injury, the claimant must obtain a medical report in accordance with paragraph 7.8C.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] 7.2 It is expected that most claimants will obtain a medical report from one expert, but additional medical reports may be obtained from other experts where the injuries require reports from more than one medical discipline.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] 7.3 The claimant must check the factual accuracy of any medical report before it is sent to the defendant.  There will be no further opportunity for the claimant to challenge the factual accuracy of a medical report after it has been sent to the defendant.

## 7.4

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (1) The medical expert should identify within the report—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (a) the medical records that have been reviewed; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (b) the medical records considered relevant to the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (2) The claimant must disclose with any medical report sent to the defendant any medical records which the expert considers relevant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.5 In most claims with a value of no more than £10,000, it is expected that the medical expert will not need to see any medical records.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.6 Any relevant photograph(s) of the claimant’s injuries upon which the claimant intends to rely should also be disclosed with the medical report.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.7 Where the claimant was not wearing a seat belt the medical report must contain sufficient information to enable the defendant to calculate the appropriate reduction of damages in accordance with principles set out in existing case law.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.8 A subsequent medical report from an expert who has already reported must be justified. A report may be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (1) the first medical report recommends that further time is required before a prognosis of the claimant’s injuries can be determined; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (2) the claimant is receiving continuing treatment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (3) the claimant has not recovered as expected in the original prognosis.

## Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] 7.8A In addition to paragraphs 7.1 to 7.7, and subject to paragraph 7.8B, in a soft tissue injury claim—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (1) the first report must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected for the claim via the MedCo Portal (website at: www.medco.org.uk (opens in a new tab) ); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (2) where the defendant provides a different account under paragraph 6.19A, the claimant must provide this as part of the instructions to the medical expert for the sole purpose of asking the expert to comment on the impact, if any, on diagnosis and prognosis if—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (a) the claimant’s account is found to be true; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (b) the defendant’s account is found to be true.

## 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (1) it is expected that only one medical report will be required;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (2) a further medical report, whether from the first expert instructed or from an expert in another discipline, will only be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (a) it is recommended in the first expert’s report; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (b) that report has first been disclosed to the defendant; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (3) where the claimant obtains more than one medical report, the first report must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected via the MedCo Portal and any further report from an expert in any of the following disciplines must also be a fixed cost medical report—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (a) Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (b) Consultant in Accident and Emergency Medicine;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (c) General Practitioner registered with the General Medical Council;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (d) Physiotherapist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council.

## Claims which consist of, or include, a claim for whiplash injury – Medical Reports

## 7.8C

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (1) The provisions of paragraph 7.8A and 7.8B apply in respect of a medical report obtained under this paragraph, save that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (a) any reference to soft tissue injury claim is to be read as referring to a claim which consists of, or includes, a claim for whiplash injury;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (b) paragraph (2) below applies in place of paragraph 7.8B(2).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (2) A further report, whether from the first expert instructed or from an expert in another discipline, will only be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (a) it is recommended in the first expert’s report;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (b) the first medical report recommends that further time is required before a prognosis of the claimant’s injuries can be determined;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (c) the claimant is receiving continuing treatment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (d) the claimant has not recovered as expected in the original prognosis.

## Non-medical expert reports

## 7.9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.9] (1) In most cases, a report from a non-medical expert will not be required, but a report may be obtained where it is reasonably required to value the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.9] (2) Paragraph 7.3 applies to non-medical expert reports as it applies to expert medical reports.

## Specialist legal advice

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Specialist legal advice] 7.10 In most cases under this Protocol, it is expected that the claimant’s legal representative will be able to value the claim. In some cases with a value of more than £10,000 (excluding vehicle related damages), an additional advice from a specialist solicitor or from counsel may be justified where it is reasonably required to value the claim.

## Witness statements

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Witness statements] 7.11 In most cases, witness statements, whether from the claimant or otherwise, will not be, required.   One or more statements may, however, be provided where reasonably required to value the claim.

## Stay of process

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stay of process] 7.12 Where the claimant needs to obtain a subsequent expert medical report or a non-medical report, the parties should agree to stay the process in this Protocol for a suitable period.  The claimant may then request an interim payment in accordance with paragraphs 7.13 to 7.16.
